To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the T cells that are recruited to the brain in response to a local inflammatory stimulus display a phenotype that is different from that of the naive cells in the draining lymph node, and are capable of binding to VCAM 2 but not to MADCAM 1.
lymphocytes infiltrating the chronically inflarmed brain have a distinctive phenotype, and bind preferentially to VCAM  1 but not MAdCAM  1.
T cells infiltrating the CNS in chronic inflammation have a distinctive phenotype and are not alpha 4 beta7 integrin high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of inflammatory cells recruited to the brain in chronic inflammation.
the nature of lymphocytes recruited to sites of inflammation.
the mechanisms that control the migration of leukocytes from the blood into the brain during inflammation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inflammatory cells in the CNS are predominantly memory T cells, but they are not the same memory T cells as are present in the lymph node, and they are not mucosal memory T cells.

the phenotype of lymphocytes recruited to sites of chronic inflammation is distinct from that of naive T cells, and that this is reflected in their adhesion molecule repertoire, and in their binding to adhesion receptors on the inflamed vascular endothelium.

the phenotype of T cells infiltrating the CNS is distinct from that of T cells in the peripheral circulation, and is consistent with the notion that these cells have been activated and are undergoing a transition from naive to memory T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phenotype of inflammatory T cells in the CNS is distinct from that of naive T cells, and resembles that of activated T cells, and that these cells bind to VCAM1 but not to the mucosal homing addressin, MAdCAM 11.

lymphocytes infiltrating the central nervous system during inflammation display a distinct phenotype and bind to vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 (VCAM 1) but not to mucosal addressin cell adhesion molecule (MAdCAM 1).

in this model of chronic CNS inflammation, T cells recruited from the blood to the CNS are memory-like cells that express high levels of CD44 and LFA 1, and low levels of CD45RA and CD45RB, and are predominantly alpha 4 beta1+ alpha 4 beta7-.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain has a unique environment and that it is not the same as the periphery.
lymphocytes recruited to inflamed brain tissue display a distinctive phenotype, and that these cells are likely to be memory T cells that are not mucosal homing.
the inflammatory T cells recruited to the CNS during experimental allergic encephalomyitis are memory T cells that express alpha 4 beta1 integrin and lack alpha E beta 7 and beta 7 integrin.
